slot_note: re-rooted 2026-11-01 at the Batch 3 queue reset: the salary-platform world (DA09) is closed; a new world, dataset and shell under the same objective and number (a state labor department's household panel survey certifying the workforce areas for a 2027 pilot)
niche: a state labor department's quarterly household employment survey certifying which workforce areas have at least 7 per cent of employed residents holding more than one job, counted as the residents would report it themselves, when a household member answers for every adult who is out when the interviewer calls
analyst_test: A strong analyst who weights the survey correctly and reads the self-report basis keeps the residents who answered for themselves and reweights them, or imputes the answered-for residents from self-reporters alike in age, sex, hours and occupation, and certifies too few areas, because the answered-for residents hold second jobs more often (the second job keeps them out when the interviewer calls) and the household member answering for them reports only about half of those jobs, which only each resident's own answers in the quarters they answered for themselves reveal.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is the prevalence of multiple jobholding on the respondent's own reporting basis, which survey methodology estimates by correcting proxy responses for their measurement error, identified in a rotating panel by the same person answering in one quarter and being answered for in another; with another field's nouns there is no household proxy respondent, no rotation panel and no reference-week second job, and the task stops reading the same.

interview start times in UTC against the state's Mountain time
workforce areas recoded from counties with one county split by ZIP
hours heaped at 40 and 'don't know' codes

stakeholder_role: chief of the labor market research office at the state labor department

spine.entity: one adult household member in one quarterly survey interview

world.geography: United States (a fictional Mountain West state)
world.org_type: state labor market information office (the state labor department's research and statistics bureau that runs the household survey)

driver: The decisive quantity is the share of a population holding a status on the basis each member would report for themselves, when members absent at the moment of measurement are reported by someone else who misses the status about half the time and holding the status is itself what makes members absent; the second-hand and first-hand reports show nearly the same share in the cross-section because the two effects offset, and only the same members' first-hand and second-hand reports in different rounds show how much the second-hand reports miss.
driver_concrete: Each workforce area's share of employed residents holding more than one job, counted as they would report it themselves: the survey answers for adults who are out at interview time through another household member, people with a second job are out at it more often, and the answering member reports a second job for only about half of those who hold one; that sensitivity is read from residents answering for themselves in one quarter and answered for in the next, and every answered-for report is corrected by it.
stump: A competent analyst who reads the act's self-report basis keeps the residents who answered for themselves and reweights them, or imputes the answered-for residents from self-reporters alike in age, sex, hours and occupation, and certifies too few areas; the answered-for residents hold second jobs more often because the second job keeps them out when the interviewer calls, and the household members answering for them report only about half of those jobs, which the cross-sectional comparison of proxy and self reports hides and only each resident's own answers across quarters reveal.

differentiation.task270: task270 v2 corrects reports members withhold because reporting costs them more than the event, a cost that moves with their position on a scale; this build corrects answers a second household member gives without knowing the status, where holding the status is what makes the member absent, and the miss rate is read within the same person across survey rounds, with no cost, threshold or behavioural response
differentiation.task192: task192 v3 carries an instrument's per-class error rates from a validation batch that covered only the window's opening; this build has no validation batch: the second-hand reporter's miss rate is identified by the same people answering for themselves in one round and being answered for in another, and the reporter is assigned by the status itself (absence), so the cross-sectional comparison of the two routes shows almost no gap

lineage.architecture: v1 (loop 0): the level's movement read across the pooled reports as the decisive rung
lineage.fate: hardened at the author's request for a second layer (2026-10-13, before any portal result); kept as rung R3 of loop 1, where the platform's employers arrive through the window paying less and the pooled movement (1.1 per cent) files $166,000
lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is a level at a reference date estimated from reports filed at earlier dates, each of which has to be carried to the reference date by how the level itself moves at a fixed grade; the reporters' own changes between their two reports run faster because individuals also climb within the grade, so carrying the reports by the paired changes overshoots and leaving them as filed undershoots.

lineage.architecture: v1 (loop 1, shipped 2026-10-13): a software company's 2027 Data Engineer pay bands from a salary-sharing platform's respondent reports, each aged to the benchmark date by the level's movement read within employers
lineage.fate: re-rooted 2026-11-01 at the Batch 3 queue reset
lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is a level at a reference date estimated from reports filed at earlier dates, each carried to the reference date by how the level itself moves at a fixed grade inside the same reporting units; the reporters' own changes between two reports run faster because individuals also climb within the grade, and the trend across the pooled reports runs slower because the units reporting at later dates sit lower, so carrying by the paired changes overshoots and carrying by the pooled trend, or not at all, undershoots.
